writeup.headline: Jabil rates Hold: strong AI-driven growth offset by thin margins, middling valuation and a weak share-price trend.
writeup.thesis: Jabil scores 61, a Hold, 4 points short of the Buy band. Growth is the standout (score 87), with latest-quarter revenue growth of 28.6% year on year, TTM revenue growth of 20.6%, and growth sped up by 16.9 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is weaker at 46, reflecting the thin margins typical of contract manufacturing: a 9.2% gross margin, 4.7% operating margin and 3.8% FCF margin, though the diluted share count is down 3.6% year on year. Valuation scores 52: P/S of 0.8x is low in absolute terms, while P/FCF of 21.8x and EV/EBIT of 18.5x are moderate, the FCF yield is 0.4 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, and overall the multiples sit near the middle of its own history. The trend score of 44 holds the rating back, with the price 24.6% below its 52-week high and shares 21.9 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days. News is supportive, led by an FY2027 outlook of $44.5 billion in revenue that reports say was above consensus.
key_risks: Thin margins leave little room for error; management expects margin gains to come late in FY2027.
Customer concentration is rising, with the largest customer at 20% of revenue and the top five at about 37%.
Heavy reliance on AI data-centre demand, targeted at about $22.1 billion of FY27 revenue, could reverse if that spending slows.
Weak price trend: price 5.3% below its 200-day average and 24.6% below its 52-week high.
P/S is more expensive than at 49 of the last 61 month-ends and EV/EBIT more expensive than at 43 of the last 61 month-ends.
what_would_change: A 4-point gain in the composite score would reach Buy, most plausibly from a recovering share-price trend (trend score 44).
Evidence of operating margin expansion toward the 6.1% core target would lift the quality score.
A drop of 17 points to below 45 would mean Sell, for example if growth faded and guidance or news turned negative.
Further gains in customer concentration or a guidance cut would weigh on the news risk score.
